utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Good morning, everybody. Welcome back, Mr. Robinson.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Mr. President, if I could just take a minute before we start. I want to advise you that I'm very happy to be back here from the ICTR in Arusha where I arrived this morning, but yesterday when I was in court the Chamber indicated that they were going to initiate contempt proceedings against me because I declined to proceed in the trial yesterday after the arrest of one of my colleagues in Rwanda who has been charged with genocide negationism. And I took the position that I couldn't represent my client because I am presenting the very same defence that he's accused of, pushing in his case, and now he's in gaol. In any event, the Chamber will eventually litigate that with me and I'm confident that I did the right thing and that I'll prevail in the end, but I wanted to inform you of that immediately and if you want to see the pleadings and the transcripts, I'm happy to provide all of that to you. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you for the information. Judge Morrison.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MORRISON
utterances.text: Mr. Robinson, I'm sorry to hear of your predicament without commenting upon it in any other way. Does that affect your position here?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: I don't think so, Judge Morrison. Hopefully I'll be entitled to the presumption of innocence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MORRISON
utterances.text: For myself, I don't see how it will affect you here. I think you've done exactly the right thing in bringing it to the Tribunal's attention in the way that you have and in the time that you have, which is a great credit to you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BAIRD
utterances.text: Mr. Robinson, let me associate myself with the views of Judge Morrison in this respect.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Judge Baird.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And I was advised that Mr. Karadzic has something to raise with the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning to everyone. Would I like to say that I'm doing everything in my power to ensure that this be an example of the way a trial should be conducted. Now, the skill with which one needs to answer questions and to focus on certain issues is something I'm gaining, getting better at from one hour to the next. So what I want to say is as far as my intentions go, they are sincere to make this an exemplary trial. However, when we look at the witnesses who testified so far, they all avoided being sincere and impartial. However, this witness in particular, what he did is -- affects the whole of the joint criminal enterprise question and the entire indictment, and I would like to request that I be given more time, because we haven't even touched upon certain matters. We've come -- we've arrived at the foundation of the Serbian Assembly in Bosnia-Herzegovina, which means that we're going to have throw light on the conduct and mind set of Radovan Karadzic first of all, and then his conduct and behaviour, and then the conduct of the whole SDS party and other Serbian parties faced with the challenge before us by the SDA party. So when I speak about the Muslim side, I'm not speaking about the Muslim people as a whole or even the whole of the SDA party but just the core according to Zulfikarpasic. So Variants A and B and the January attempt to save Bosnia and preserve peace, the March Cutileiro conference, and then we have -- well, we haven't even touched upon the question of the roots of responsibility in the words of the deputies and Karadzic in the Assembly. So we have to throw light and elucidate that whole situation, and then we come to the whole question of Sarajevo. So it was a real surprise when I heard that I won't even have 20 of the 40 hours that I had initially asked for. So I do wish to apologise for my lack of experience, but I am gaining that experience and becoming more efficacious in my cross-examination. But this is that kind of witness. He is expanding on the subjects and areas and bringing me into a situation whereby I have to deal with the new elements he brought up. So I have to struggle and show that with a he's saying is not correct. There's nothing that this witness has not touched upon. So I had to take that up. He goes into all the words and sentences stated by people, which are not really relevant because they don't exist in any document, but he is accusing me of things on that basis, and I'm afraid that the Trial Chamber will not be able to understand the mind-set of Radovan Karadzic or his conducts or indeed the entire crisis unless this witness is kept here at our disposal so that we can challenge everything he has designed and redesigned and reshaped to suit him and which we have to deal with. So I do take on board all your criticisms about my cross-examination techniques, but there is no lawyer in the world that can know the facts as I know them. I know exactly what happened there, and I know exactly where his report is erroneous, and, in fact, his books differ from his expert report. There's more truth in the books he wrote than in the report he wrote for the OTP. So that is what I wanted to say, and I'd like to you to believe me when I say that I have every good intention but that it is necessary for me to clear up all the topics that this witness has raised, because they can all be important when it comes to judgement day.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: While you have so many important and relevant issues you just referred to, you wasted your time for the first few days concentrating on only marginally relevant issues, making open-ended questions, making comments without adhering to our advice. But having observed your conduct of your cross-examination yesterday, we are convinced that you are able to ask the relevant questions in an efficient way, complying with the guidance given by the Chamber. So we are confident you can conduct your cross-examination in such a manner, so we are confident you will be able to finish your cross-examination in a -- in not so long a period of time. So please concentrate your -- on conducting your cross-examination on relevant questions, and if you do not waste your time and you are concentrating on relevant issues and then at the end of the day if you have still remaining legitimate issues, the Chamber will consider the situation again. That does not mean that you are at liberty to ask any questions. That said, let's bring in the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MORRISON
utterances.text: Dr. Karadzic, simply as an addendum to that which the President has said and as the President has said, it's perfectly apparent that your technique has improved considerably; but if you concentrate purely on those matters which pertain to the indictment, which is really what is the concern of the Tribunal, I think you will find that even though you've talked about a number issues you'll find that what really matters, certainly as far as the Tribunal is concerned, are those matters which are directly related to the indictment. As far as any other peripheral and historic matters are concerned, you'll be free to deal with those, of course, yourself in due course, and as far as the written material is concerned, that's a matter for the Court to draw inferences from in any event. So it's -- even if there are matters which you feel that you ought to put to Dr. Donia but don't, don't think that's the end of the matter, because you won't be precluded from raising those issues in due course in any event.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you, Judge Morrison. Mr. Karadzic. Good morning, Doctor.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Let's continue.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Good morning, Dr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Once again, good morning to everybody. And may I have 65 ter 11452 on e-court, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And while we're waiting for that to come up, let me ask you, Mr. Donia, do you know of a document -- well, do you know what the Serbs are proposing and proposed in a document that was officially published in the summer of 1991?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what you're referring to, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: It's a document in which the Serbian Democratic Party and associated other parties, and there are several of them, parliamentary ones as well, are proposing how the Yugoslav crisis should be resolved. It's is very important document by which the Serbs legitimised, if I can put it that way, their position and announced their position and standpoint.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, I'm told that document hasn't been uploaded in the e-court. Yes, Ms. Edgerton. Good morning to you.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honour. And if I could for the record note that my senior trial attorney, Ms. Uertz-Retzlaff has joined us today, please. Could I suggest that we turn to 65 ter 00942, and I think Dr. Karadzic will find there the document he's requested.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Edgerton.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Here we have it, Dr. Donia. We have a publication in two languages in July, published and distributed already in July, what the Serbs propose, and the views of the Serbian Democratic Party, and of course those who supported us as well, about a solution to the Yugoslav, and by the same token the Bosnian and Herzegovinian crisis. Are you aware and familiar with this document?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Now that I look at it, yes, I have seen it before. I seem -- I recall that it was associated with or came out of the meeting of the 12th of July, the St. Peter and Paul's Day meeting, but that may be wrong. But I do recognise the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I don't think it was linked to any meeting but negotiations. And can we see the next page, please. Into the text. These are all the title pages, but into the text. And the English version, please. May we have the English version. Can you read this, Professor Donia?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Give me some time and I'll be glad to.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: If you want me to, I can read it out, but we don't have the English version.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: No, I think the English version seems to be at the end of the document. I'm checking.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: The document is in two languages itself. That's why there's no independent translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. Can we take a look at page 8 in e-court.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is the introduction. May we move on and see what the Serb side proposed. The signatories are Radovan Karadzic and the president of the deputies' club, Professor Maksimovic. Now, let's see what the initial positions are of the Serb side with respect to a resolution of the Yugoslav crisis and the place of Bosnia-Herzegovina in Yugoslavia. Take a look at that last page in the chapter positions: "[In English] It is therefore necessary for all Yugoslav institutions, the Presidency, the Assembly and the government to function because final agreement on the democratic organisation or relations in Yugoslavia must be verified in these Yugoslav institutions." [Interpretation] And so be and so forth. Now, may we turn to the next page, please. Number 2: "[In English] The original sovereignty belongs unquestionably to the citizens and peoples. The citizens and peoples realise their sovereignty partly in their respective republics which are regulated by the republican constitutions and partly in the federal state which is regulated by the federal constitution." [Interpretation] So that I don't have to read it all out, can I draw your attention to this document, take a look at it -- or, rather, perhaps you could take a look at this during our first break, and I recommend this document to the Trial Chamber because it was one of the more important documents, official proposals, for a solution to the crisis, and I'm afraid that without this document and, in fact, I'm very surprised that you haven't received this document because without it you cannot understand the Serb positions. Now, shall I tender it into evidence later once Dr. Donia has had a chance to look through the document or should I do that now?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: What is your question, Dr. Karadzic?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, Dr. Donia, do you consider this to be an important document, the substance of which must have been taken into consideration when you wrote your expert report.

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just from what I have seen so far, I don't see anything striking about it. I don't see a significant change from the party's previous position. I think the -- I would again suggest that the context in which it was issued probably was important and perhaps called for a restatement of some of these views, and that context was, of course, that the Federal Presidency had refused to confirm Mr. Mesic in the position of president of the Presidency on May 15th, and so the Presidency was in effect deadlocked at the time that the independence declarations were issued by Slovenia and Croatia on the 25th of -- of June, and of course that was followed by the ten-day war in Slovenia and the agreement reached at Brioni which specified, among other things, that Mr. Mesic would be installed in that -- in that post. Now, I assume that all that required some restatement here of the principles of what the -- what the party wanted, but as I say, don't see -- I don't see anything striking about this relative to some of the earlier positions of the party.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But, Mr. Donia, do you agree that this is a document in which the party's going public as a Serb proposal? Would that be right?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not -- I don't know who -- who signed it or who prepared it, so I don't see -- again, I don't see anything here that would have been in the public domain for the first time, but I have not had a chance to review the entire document, so I wouldn't want to say that definitively.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Can we go to the last page.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You have the members of the Presidency signed there, Professor Plavsic, Professor Koljevic, party President Karadzic, and President of the Serbian members of parliament club, Professor Maksimovic. So there you have the party and the top representatives, Serb representatives, in the government bodies. This is an official platform for a solution to the crisis, and I think that it merits a place in your report, at least as a mention, as an aside, if nothing more.

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I did not -- I have reviewed this document previously but didn't feel that it brought anything riveting to -- to change the picture.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Take a look at this paragraph: "[In English] Cantonal territories are not all embracing for there are also enclaves and separate local communities surrounded by a territory to which they do not belong. This is especially frequent in the boundary regions of the French and German speaking cantons. This principle is particularly applicable to the ethnically analogous areas in Yugoslavia." [Interpretation] Do you remember that we proposed that -- or, rather that, we supported a proposal coming from Croatia that wherever the conditions existed, cantons should be founded and that they did not have to have any territorial links?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not certain at what level -- that proposal was certainly floating around and was favourably -- the SDS was favourably disposed to it. I don't know that it ever reached the level of an agreement with anyone, Croats or anyone else, or whether it was advanced in specific negotiations. It -- very familiar and really fully consistent with -- with where the party was at that point in time in -- in supporting what I call the -- the municipal strategy.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you remember that we put this paper aside because the MBO came out with a propose that will there should be no regionalisation and that Bosnian should remain in Yugoslavia, the so-called historical Muslim-Serb agreement, July, August 1991. Yes or no?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I hear a couple questions there. I don't know that you set this proposal aside. I didn't see it retracted. Certainly events with -- with the proposals made by Messrs. Filipovic and Zulfikarpasic, it was to be sure superseded in many respects, probably more than anything else put at a second priority position, but I don't know that it was ever set aside.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You see, I claim and put it to you that this proposal kept the peace in Yugoslavia and Bosnia-Herzegovina, and I also claim that the next proposal that came from Zulfikarpasic and Filipovic to give up on the creation of cantons, to abolish that idea on the basis of the Serbian-Muslim agreement, also preserved the peace in Yugoslavia and Bosnia-Herzegovina and that they are two possibilities both of which the Serbs accepted. One they proposed, the other they accepted. Yes or no?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'd like to tender this document now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit D288.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Can we have the date when this was published.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] At the beginning of July 1991, before the negotiations on the historical Serb-Muslim agreement started.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Could we have 65 ter 30249, please. 65 ter 30249, and this is the 19th of September, a conversation between Karadzic and Dr. Vukic, who was in Banja Luka, and in the Banja Luka Krajina or Bosnian Krajina he was the head of the SDS there. May we look at page 2 of that, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Let me remind you Krajina itself alone proclaimed itself to be an autonomous region after Izetbegovic rejected the Serb-Muslim peace agreement. Now let's see what it says here.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Second page in English, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Dr. Vuk says: "[In English] However, it goes on --" [Interpretation] And he says that they proclaimed the region and so on, and so this can go. And then Karadzic says: "[In English] All right. [Interpretation] All right. [In English] Well --" And then he says: "No referendum is needed for that. It is in accordance with what we are agreeing upon with Izetbegovic, only that Izetbegovic we are afraid that they want to cheat us on us because Izetbegovic is saying one thing and Silajdzic in The Hague is saying something different, and that is why you did the right thing to proclaim it, and that is why I did not resist it. However, we shall sit and make a deal with them to what the Muslims have a right to in the Serb regions and what the Serbs have a right to in the Muslim regions, but we shall agree on everything." Dr. Donia, don't you see that I did not initiate this but I did not oppose the proclamation of the Autonomous Region of the Krajina, and I confirm that we were negotiating such matters with Izetbegovic?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I think the history of the Serbian autonomous regions would say otherwise. The Serbian Democratic Party made the decision to proclaim these regions in early September and over the next month and a half they were, in fact, proclaimed more or less one by one. In -- I think on the 16th, if I'm not mistaken, 16th of September, the community of municipalities of the Bosnian Krajina effectively transformed itself into this -- what's frequently called the ARK, the autonomous region of Krajina, which gave it a slightly different title than the other SAOs and in a sense made it first among equals. This appeared to me to be in conjunction with the overall effort to proclaim these SAOs on a large part of Bosnian territory.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I'm asking you about this answer. Can one not see on the basis of this answer that they had proclaimed it? I did not initiate it. I simply didn't resist it. Second question: Do you not see here that what is envisaged is the existence of minorities and the regulation of their rights?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That -- you're asking about the sentence, "That is why you did right to proclaim it. That is why I did not resist it"? Yes, it says that. So, true. My understanding of the development was somewhat different from what you state here, but certainly you did explain it in those terms here. And you hope to make a deal about regions with Muslims, and that's, I think, also clear from the -- from the text here.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You, yourself, had confirmed that I fought a fierce battle with the regions, telling them to wait and to be behave in accordance with the negotiations. The initiatives were theirs, but I was trying to put a brake on them as it were.

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think on this question you have to be very careful about what time you're talking about. I think you fought a fierce battle with the people in the ARK -- or the ZOBK in June, late June and early July when they proclaimed the union of the two Krajinas, and then that issue kind of receded for a while as other events took centre stage, and it really was not again until the -- I think the events in December of 1991 when the question arose of the character of the Serbian state that was about to be proclaimed, should include in the view the people in the Krajina, an autonomous or even separate polity for the Krajina. So I view this struggle that you had with the people in Krajina as probably the biggest challenge that you faced in unifying the party, but it was intermittent, and at this particular time I don't view it as -- my own research wouldn't suggest that it was a particularly acute issue.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this document be admitted?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that in the first sentence we quoted I'm saying they should not call a referendum because that is in accordance with what we are negotiating with Izetbegovic; right?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I believe you also told someone else, about this time, that you didn't think you'd get the -- you'd win a referendum in the Bosnian Krajina. So, yes, I agree. You were trying to avoid a referendum going forward in the Bosnian Krajina on this issue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We'll mark it for identification.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As MFI D289, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We do have a translation, Excellency. Oh, I see. Because it's an intercept. I agree. Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Dr. Donia, do you agree that I had said we cannot count on being able to get a two-thirds majority of the referendum and that is why we cannot win at a referendum?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And do you remember that I said that that pertained to all of Krajina, because in Cazinska Krajina, in Bihac there are 300.000 Muslims and the Serb population in Krajina is about 5- or 600.000.

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall what the unit of analysis was that you were talking about. I don't recall it from memory. It was in another telephone intercept, and I don't recall the specific number of municipalities or area that you were speaking of.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. May I remind you that we objected to the SDA that constitutional decisions cannot be made by a simple majority. Everything that had to do with the constitution required a two-thirds majority because that was prescribed by the constitution; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Edgerton.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: That was comment, with respect, Your Honour, and I also suggest that as soon as I took to my feet, Dr. Karadzic concluded his comment with the question, "Isn't that right."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I understood that to be the question. But be careful, Mr. Karadzic. There's no need on your part to remind the witness of something. You can ask questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. If I could also observe. It might be better for the Prosecution to wait until he has completed his question before making an objection, because I think it's very fair to ask a question at the end of the sentence rather as well as --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Let's not waste time.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I understand that you're not a constitutional expert, but you do recall that that was our position. That's why I asked you whether you recall that our position was that constitutional matters had to be resolved on the basis of the constitution, that is to say about a two-third majority.

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not always, and I think depended on the particular body that you were -- you were dealing with at the time. Clearly you did not have that position in Municipal Assemblies where in many cases the votes to join the community of municipalities of the Bosnian Krajina were by simple majority votes or in some cases even contested. When the other parties raised the objection that those votes should be by two-thirds vote, the SDS delegates rejected that position and voted them into the ZOBK by simple majority. Now, that's one example of a body that the two-thirds rule was not insisted on, in fact, was resisted by the SDS. I would certainly agree that you felt that way about issues voted upon in the -- in the Assembly, in the parliament of Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Am I right when I say that when a change in the association of municipalities takes place it does not mean a change in the constitution? It is simply a change by law and that requires simply a simple majority.

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, of course, you always had an opinion on what was constitutional and what was not constitutional, and you may have felt that this was just a matter of law, but the situation in which I just cited, the representatives of the HDZ and SDA felt that it was a matter of constitutional procedure. So you had one view of that, and the members of the other parties had a different view of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now have 65 ter 07288 in e-court, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: We are going to cast a brief glance, so there is an English translation. Could I have page 34 in English. These are stenographic notes from the Assembly meeting that you mentioned on the 12th of July, 1991. The second page in Serbian, please. Page 27, actually, in Serbian, and 34 in English. Twenty-seven in Serbian, and 34 in English. We need the next page in Serbian. This is 26, and we need 27. This is my response to Dr. Vukic that pertains precisely to this issue. I would like to draw your attention to my words: "Those who will attend our afternoon session will be able to hear a part of last year's report in which we presented a general objection to the regionalisation and territorialisation of Bosnia-Herzegovina after the war which had been carried out consistent to the detriment of the Serbian people. Thus the idea of the re-regionalisation of Bosnia-Herzegovina --" Can we have the next page in English please -- "Has been present from the very outset among the founders and creators of the SDS ideas -- founders and creators of the SDS ideas from the very start, and the Main Board has always taken that into account and members of the Main Board and then regions." Page 35 in English: "The regions that we envisage, that we proclaimed as communities and municipalities within the framework of the BiH constitution, are not socio-political communities yet at this point in time. In order for them to become that we have to go through the BiH Assembly so that there is a law that says that such and such a region is not only a community of municipalities but a socio-political community with all the elements after full political life." Dr. Donia, can we not see on the basis of this that they are irrelevant, these associations of municipalities, but in the Assembly if -- or, rather if they become regions, then in the Assembly we have to ensure on the basis of a law that these regions have a political life.

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I regard this passage as actually part of the evidence for the process that was going on in the aftermath of the proclamation of the union of the two Krajinas, which roil your own sense of what should be done and resulted in a strong effort by the party to make sure that that actually was not carried out. And I take it what you're taking here is that it is time to put this whole issue of regionalisation under the Main Board as it was originally, that basically the ideas for regionalisation, the proposals for regionalisation came from the Main Board of the party, or, at the very least, members of the Main Board of the party. And it was now important to, in a sense, re-centralise the party -- party's control over this process and make sure that it proceeded in a way that was consistent with the party's overall objectives. I think it's -- I'm a little bit puzzled by the references to the Bosnian Assembly, because as you cited yesterday, the Bosnian Assembly had already passed a recommendation that the formation of the community of municipalities of Bosnian Krajina not go forward. So the Assembly had already staked out its position on this, and of course that recommendation did nothing to deter the process that moved forward of creating the ZOBK.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Yesterday we established that that was the recommendation that was there, not to give up on it but to wait until the Yugoslav crisis is resolved. However, we see here that it does not have much importance, and it doesn't really have any powers. However, for the region to start life of its own we intend to deal with it through the Assembly of Bosnia-Herzegovina so that it is regulated by law, not by constitution but by law; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I'd have to hear that question again. I wasn't clear what you were asking.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You see what I said, and, on the basis of that, it means that associations of municipalities have not become socio-political communities. They do not have powers of their own. They cannot pass regulations, and they cannot function as a municipality can function. So a municipality is more important than an association of municipalities. Are we trying to deal with this through a parliamentary procedure, not to change the constitution but to change the law. Can you not see that that is our intention, to have regions legalised by passing relevant laws through the Assembly; right?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. From this it would suggest that your view was that raising the status of a community of municipalities to the highest level of an organisation, socio-political community, could be done simply by a law in the Assembly. Yeah, that's your view expressed here.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we have page 36 in English. I have before me the recommendation that we saw yesterday. It says it is recommended that they stop all decisions concerning regionalisation while negotiations are underway on the constitutional crisis in Yugoslavia. 6225 that's what we adopted yesterday. So it is not declared unlawful. The political recommendation is that we have a standstill before the political crisis is resolved. It should be page 29 in Serbian, I think. And you see my words here again: "We will not create. We will not create anything that is in the constitution for as long as the constitution exists." That is imprecise, and then I say further on: "However, everything we have done so far we have done within the framework of the constitution of BiH and Yugoslavia." If someone violates the constitutions of BiH and Yugoslavia then we no longer have any obligations towards the constitution and then we are going to do what Mr. Vukic and Mr. Kupresanin have announced. So others have -- another party has to violate the BiH constitution to try to affect the secession of Bosnia-Herzegovina, and if they do so then we will prepare a democratic response of the Serbian people on all lies and in every respect. Can you not see that I am advocating observance of the constitution for as long as it exists?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think you're saying here that you're arrogating unto yourself the decision about whether any particular act is unconstitutional, and should you deem an act to be unconstitutional, then all bets are off and the party can go and organise whatever it wants to in response. That's again -- the interpretation of constitutionality here you place wholly in your hands with this statement, and given that proviso, I agree with what you've just formulated, that actions won't be taken until someone else violates the constitution first, and that was very consistent with your position at that time and even earlier in the party.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can this document be admitted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I note it already has been admitted as Exhibit D273.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's possible. Thank you. 30243. Can we have that, please. That's the 65 ter number. 65 ter 30243. The date is the 18th of September, so all of this is September. The beginning of the second half of September.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So this is a conversation between Karadzic and Brdjanin, Brdjanin and Karadzic. So can we see the next page. So they have proclaimed the Autonomous Region of the Krajina, and now they are discussing the referendum, and I'm saying: "All right. Look. You don't need any kind of referendum. All of your decisions are lawful." And he says, "Oh, really." And then the next sentence or rather, paragraph: "Well, yes, why would you expose yourself to some kind of risks and expenses? I am negotiating with Alija. All of that is in accordance with this. Now it is a question of whether they're going to be called Serb or whether they were not -- will not be called Serb." It's the second page in English as well. "Whether they will be called Serb or whether they will not be called Serb." Sorry. The third page in English. Is it? The third. Yes. "[In English] Yes, why would you expose --" [Interpretation] And now the next page. "[In English] Serbian will not be called Serbian." [Interpretation] Now on the next page: "Whether they will be called Serb or whether they will not be called Serb, will there be any exaggerations or not. Where will the borders run of one and where will the borders of the other run?"

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, I'm not sure the doctor is able follow. Let's locate the relevant page first.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The bottom of the second page in English and then it continues on the third page.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, I see the passage.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I'm saying: "All right. Listen, you don't need any referendum. All of your decisions are legal," and then I say, "But I am negotiating with Alija. All of that is in keeping with this. The question remains whether they will be called Serbian or whether they will not be called Serbian, whether they -- whether anyone will push matters too far or not, where the borders of one or the other will run." The next page in English then: "How much of the legislative power will belong to the region? How much to the republic? How much to the joint state? I mean everything he talked about on television last night has fallen through. Yesterday after the news programme we talked and reached an agreement, that is in keeping with our agreement. Regionalisation is on and the reason is our side is going faster is that your Silajdzic is acting differently in Europe, in The Hague." So I'm trying to dissuade the people of Krajina. It is unnecessary, because talks are being held with Izetbegovic. They are underway. However, Silajdzic is saying something completely different in Europe and that is what we were afraid of. You know that at the time Silajdzic and Izetbegovic were in the same party. Remember that.

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm wondering what the question was.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: The question was whether Silajdzic and Izetbegovic were in the same party at the time.

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they were both in the SDA.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can one see on the basis of this that Izetbegovic is negotiating one thing with us and Silajdzic is saying completely different at the conference in The Hague?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't view this -- I don't view your representation here as -- as authoritative on the positions that Mr. Silajdzic and Mr. Izetbegovic were taking at the time, and the -- the suggestion here that they were somehow clambering on board with the idea of regionalisation in particular the formation of the SAOs seems to me to be completely wrong. The -- I know that at some point the Presidency of Bosnia-Herzegovina, at least its majority, over two-thirds majority, denounced the formation of the SAOs, and I believe the government did as well in a Resolution. So it was the position of the SD -- yeah, of the SDA and the HDZ at that time in -- they were completely opposed to this measure. There may have been some talks going on, but, certainly at the time we're talking about, they were condemning it rather than looking to resolve the -- whatever conflict might exist about the specific nature of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Please have a look at this sentence: "Last night," that is to say Izetbegovic and I, "were on the news programme the previous evening. Yesterday after the news programme we talked and we reached an agreement. That is in accordance with our agreement. Regionalisation is underway." So, Mr. Donia, are you trying to say that I'm lying, that I am telling Brdjanin a lie, that I had agreed with Izetbegovic that regionalisation should go on?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it's very possible, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Can we have this document admitted for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D290, Your Honours. I apologise, MFI D290.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: May we now have 1D1422 next, please. There should be an English translation. There it is. Now let's have a look and see which party is preparing. Well, they made the proclamation, and they say: "Looking at the report on the needs and possibilities of the territorial organisation of Banja Luka municipality and the founding of Banja Luka-Stari Grad municipality is adopted in its entirety the SDA, HDZ, SDS, SDP and Liberal Party of Banja Luka at a meeting held on the 24th of October, 1991, issues the following proclamation: The analysis of the needs and possibility for the territorial organisation of Banja Luka municipality and the founding of Banja Luka-Stari Grad, Old Town municipality, is adopted in its entirety, and a transformation of the present municipality of Banja Luka and the six municipalities is proposed as follows:" And then it goes on to enumerate the municipalities. Do you see that the question of territorial reorganisation for the municipalities in Bosnia-Herzegovina is being considered at all levels without necessarily thinking about secession from Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could we go to the second page of this document?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, please. By all means. I see no signature there.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: In B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Right. This is a -- actually, we referred to this briefly yesterday. This is a proposal, and it's in the form that is -- was often submitted for consideration by a legislative body, prepared by one of the parties, and usually that -- the party that prepared the proposal would have its name first and then space would be left for the presidents of the parties to sign if, indeed, an agreement was reached. This was the -- indeed the propose of the SDA to break up this large Banja Luka municipality into five units and providing very specific boundaries of it. I can tell you from press reports that this died a sudden death shortly after it was proposed and was rolled out with great fanfare by a spokesman for the SDA I believe sometime in late September, maybe as late as November of 1991, and then won the support of no one else, and it appeared that even the central party of the SDA in Sarajevo distanced itself from it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, many proposals fell through, Mr. Donia. Do you agree that the events put lots of proposals to one side? There might have been proposals, but the developments pushed them to one side; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I couldn't agree more, and so many of the proposals that you have been showing to me in the last several days died a similar death. They failed to reach the level of agreement necessary to be formally adopted and fell by the wayside.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But you're not challenging the fact that they were conducting negotiations and that the process was ongoing; right?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would agree that negotiations were ongoing again perhaps intermittently but throughout the period we're considering here, that is, at least up until, say, the 24th of October.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, do you see here in the Serbian version, I don't know whether you can see that in the English, that citizens are called in all municipalities, villages, and so on, to state their views about the founding of each of these municipalities. So the local communes were the basic unit to decide which municipality they would belong to; right?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The SDA terminology was most frequently to use "citizens" and that was their proposal here, that citizens vote.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I'd like to tender this document now and call up document 1421 next, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit D291.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: 1D1421 next, please. And here we have the statutory decision of a group of citizens of the local communes of Banja Luka, Hiseta, Majdan, Gornji Seher, et cetera. The meeting of the citizens of the local communes and then the communes are enumerated and they're mostly Muslim populated local communes?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. Can you set -- establish the date first. Is it November, Doctor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I believe it to be November, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Continue, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So this is a continuation of the previous document, the previous action that was taken. These local communes did as was proposed and brought in a statutory decision on the organisation of the Stari Grad-Banja Luka municipal Assembly and the founding. Article 1, the municipality of Stari Grad-Banja Luka is a basic democratic, socio-political community of equal citizens, nations, and nationalities living in it. And can we look at the last page now, please. Last page in English, please, as well. Last page in the English. The penultimate, before this diagram. It's a diagram of the local communes but that's the one we need and Article 21: "This decision enters into force on the date of its adoption." And it was signed by the president of the working Presidency, Dr. Sead Hadzagic, and you know what our circumstances were like, and you can judge by the name and say that it's a Muslim; right?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think your representation about the nature of this document is -- is false. This was a draft of a resolution that would have been adopted by the individual municipal or local Assemblies had it, in fact, passed the Banja Luka Assembly. This was very common at the time. The same thing was done, actually, in the formation of the ZOBK where there was a boilerplate resolution put together for the local communes to use in actually declaring themselves a member of the ZOBK. This is essentially the same thing in an individual copy. It is not signed by Dr. Hadzagic. It is type script and it would not have been signed without having actually been enacted through the actions of the bodies concerned.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: May we have the first page displayed again, please, and you'll see that that's not the case. Here it says at a meeting of the 17th of November 1991 the following statutory decision was taken. So what was up to the local communes they did. They fulfilled their obligation. They passed the statutory decision to form an Assembly like that. So from there point of view they did everything they needed to do and then further procedure was necessary in the municipality. So this is a decision. The decision was made on the 17th of November. It's a final decision following recommendations from the previous document. Does it say, Has taken the following decision? And does it refer to the document, the previous document I mean.

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I think without a -- without a signature and without actual publication in the Official Gazette, this does not represent evidence of what you have you've said it is, that the action is actually even taken.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I tender this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit D292.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May we have 1D1419 next, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: This is a document dated the 12th of November, Studeni. The SDA document was the 17th. Here we have the 12th of November, and they are conclusions from a joint meeting of the Herzegovina regional community and the Travnik regional community organised by the HDZ, the Croatian Democratic Union. So we have two Croatian regions here, predominantly populated by Croats. Two regions meeting. And the first sentence says: On the 12th of November, Studeni, the Croatian town for November 1991, a working meeting was held, attended by the presidents of the Crisis Staffs of the Herzegovina regional community and the presidents of the Crisis Staffs of the Travnik regional community was held and the following conclusions were reached. Did you know about this document?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, do I.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And did you also know that already at that time they had Crisis Staffs?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think these were formed within a few days prior to this, but did I know that there were Crisis Staffs at the time that these declarations were actually issued, yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did the Serbs have Crisis Staffs at that same time?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. May we now see -- well, let's look at the conclusions and start off with the sentence that reads in Busovaca it was unanimously decided that the Croatia people in Bosnia-Herzegovina must finally wage a joint active policy which should lead to the realisation of our centuries-old dream of a joint Croatian state. For this historical goal to become a reality soon these two regional communities request the commencement of activities to formulate an issue, legal and political documents, the proclamation of a Croatian Banovina in Bosnia-Herzegovina, a referendum on -- I can't see that word, that next word. On -- on accession to the Republic of Croatia, et cetera. Did you know that this conclusion was reached?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is kind of standard fare, I think. It's the origins or the beginning of a split within the HDZ of Bosnia-Herzegovina in which one group, which was more under President Tudjman's sponsorship, declared these regions within Bosnia. Many people at the time viewed them as a response to your declaration of the Serbian autonomous regions and referred to them as HAOs, Croatian autonomous regions. And, in fact, at the end of the day they declared, I think, on the 19th of November, the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna, which I'm sure you have a document on coming up here, and attempted to delineate territorially their claims to this autonomous area of Bosnia very similar to what you had done with the SAOs.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you mean to say that the Croats were afraid of Serb hegemony and did this because of the Serbs and not because of the Muslims and Muslim hegemony; is that what you're trying to say?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I think that the wing of the party that was closest to Tudjman was worried about you getting too far ahead of them in staking out territorial claims in Bosnia. There are some differences, but basically they were working to be sure that their claims were taken note of very shortly after your own claims were staked out in the formation of the SAOs. I think the primary purpose of both was to marginalise or eliminate -- reduce to the lowest -- least area possible that area which would be subject to Muslim territorial claims should they seek to advance them.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: May we now turn to the next page of this document, please. And while we're waiting for that, let me ask you this, Dr. Donia: You talk about two wings of the HDZ. When did the HDZ divide and separate into two parts, parties?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not speak of two wings of the party. I said it was a split within the party, a split on viewpoints, and never did formally divide. In early February 1992, the leadership of Stjepan Kljujic was -- Stjepan Kljujic and his immediate followers were purged at a meeting of the HDZ. I believe it was in Grude or Siroki Brijeg. And that represented the kind of final triumph of this separatist wing within the party. But in the meantime, until that happened, there were people of differing views inhabiting the same party and having some pretty serious disputes about which approach to take. Also note, however, that when this announcement of Herceg-Bosna was made, it was made without the prior knowledge of Mr. Kljujic who was president of the party. He was holding a press conference in Sarajevo and learned from a reporter about the proclamation and did his best to disguise the fact that it was a complete surprise to him and, in fact, ended up sort of tepidly endorsing the proclamation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I'd like to draw the participants' attention to points (b) and (c) of item 3. Launch political and legal actions on the democratic scene and internationally and (c) preparing better military for clashes with all those forces which will try to stop this inevitable process in the establishment of free Croatian state. That then is the 12th of November. When was the decision taken to form Republika Srpska? Do you remember that? Do you agree that it was the 9th of January, 1992?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think the name Republika Srpska was adopted in August of 1992. The republic of the Serbian people of Bosnia-Herzegovina was proclaimed on January 9.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I tender this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: What is your question about clause (b) and (c)? You just read out without posing a question.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well I think I did ask a question. Dr. Donia answered and said that he knew about this document knew about this process. Now, his interpretation is one I don't agree with but never mind. He knows it was a process and that this line or stream within the HDZ prevailed and that Kljujic lost. So the question was, in fact, was this process -- or, rather, did Dr. Donia take into account this process that happened in Bosnia-Herzegovina among the Croatian population.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I did. I think it's described in not great detail but in a paragraph or two in my -- one of the reports that has been submitted for this case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. With the question and answer we'll have a break for 20 minutes. Before that we'll admit this one.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, Exhibit D293.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Before you begin, Mr. Karadzic, Judge Baird has something to say to you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BAIRD
utterances.text: Dr. Karadzic, before we continue with your cross-examination, may I say something here. I fully agree with the comments of my colleagues that your cross-examination yesterday was clearly in keeping with the guidelines the Chamber gave you sometime earlier. Your technique and the quality of your cross-examination yesterday left nothing to be desired, but today you seem to be reverting back to the original situation where your questions don't appear to be impacting, generally speaking, on the indictment. Now, be it admitted that the Chamber is not aware of the details of your defence, you alone would know what you want to explore and what you want to establish, and, indeed, I just said that this morning you are making some progress. I mean, there's no two ways about that. But it would be good if you could continue in the vein that you adopted yesterday in your cross-examination: Succinct questions, pertinent questions, no comment. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Excellency. I'll do my utmost to follow those guidelines. May I now call up on e-court --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the microphones be switched off, please, that aren't in use. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- 11365, next document, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that the Serb side saw the Assembly, the Assembly meeting of the 14th and 15th of October very dramatically, 1991?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I think actually all sides did.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I'm not -- 11306 is the correct document number. I don't know if I misspoke earlier on. That's not the document, so may we have 11306, please. Dr. Donia, these are notes from the council of the Serbian Democratic Party, but before that let me ask you a question. Do you remember that the council was first established as a council for inter-party co-operation?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Headed by Professor Koljevic, I believe, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And that there were some prominent people, members of it, who weren't members of the SDS to begin with; right?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And also that Mrs. Plavsic, Professor Plavsic, as a member of the council was nominated although she was a party member, but she was nominated.

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wasn't aware of that. I note that at this meeting there were a number of party members there, too, so it wasn't clear to me at the meeting that we're talking about who was actually on the council and who was not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Is that the document you're going to tender?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: It says Exhibit -- no, no.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honour, the 65 ter number is 00962.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, Ms. Edgerton.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: I was standing up for two reasons, Your Honour. Exactly that which my friend has indicated, and this is not a document we've been notified on.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do believe that Dr. Donia mentions this document somewhere in his report, to the best of my recollections.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But let me ask you: Are you familiar with these minutes from the party council session?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Whether or not Dr. Donia mentioned on this document is a separate matter from the fact that you have to inform the other party of the documents you're going to use during your cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes I agree, but unfortunately we don't have an enough members on our team, but may we continue.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your question was, I believe, am I familiar with the document, and yes I am.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Here the president of the council was Professor Slavko Leovac, a member of the academy.

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I'd like to draw your attention, and everybody else's, to what Mr. Najdavov says -- Najdanovic. The Muslims are in hurry to adopt the declaration because of The Hague conference, but they are also in a hurry because of the strong pressure by the Croatian leadership which wants to reduce the pressure of the army on Croatia by opening up a front in Bosnia-Herzegovina. Do you remember that Stjepan Mesic, who was at the time -- well, he wasn't president of Croatia but a member of the of Presidency said that the war would spill over from Croatia into Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember the specific verb he used, whether it would or might or there existed a possibility of. I certainly remember he made some -- raised the possibility that war would spill from Croatia into Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, would you -- I'd like to draw your attention to the third sentence from the reply made by academician Milorad Ekmecic, who was one of the most respected and prominent of our historians; right?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Certainly, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And what he proposes here is this: Therefore, we should continue our contacts with the leadership of the Croatian Democratic Union and the Party of Democratic Action in our search for a political solution. The Serbs have created regions which are not interconnected, and these regions must not be allowed to establish their governments which would not be interconnected. May we turn to the next page, please, so that we can go through the whole document first and then I'll come to my questions. Well, in English it was actually the first page. So page 2 for the Serbian but back to page 1 for the English. Back to page one for the English, please. Do you remember that Todor Dutina, who at that time was in the Reformist Party of Ante Markovic went on to make the next statement and Kecmanovic too. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Do you recall what, his statement or -- or --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: That he was a reformist at the time. He became an SDS party member only during the war.

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't -- I didn't know prior to now what his party affiliation was at the time of this meeting, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Let's see what Mr. Dutina proposes. You know, that Dutina was otherwise a writer. He was also Bosnian's ambassador after the war; right?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Number 1 it says: "Issue a proclamation addressed to the Party of Democratic Action, the Croatian Democratic Union (the leadership) asking them to withdraw within seven days from the decision they have adopted, otherwise the Serbian Democratic Party will instruct its members to leave the existing government institutions and begin creating parallel ones. " Now, I'm sure you know that frequently when there is a parliamentary crisis the people would leave the various government institutions. Do you agree?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not always. Sometimes they stayed in government institutions. Sometimes some people left and others stayed. I wouldn't make that a general conclusion, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now let's see what Professor Koljevic has to say. With the Party of Democratic Action and the Croatian Democratic Union, we can do nothing -- nothing can be done legally. And let's see what Mitar Miljanovic goes on to say. He says the strategic goal of those confronting us is the creation of autonomy followed by republic and ultimately a Jamahirija. And Velibor Ostojic says the party policy, up to now, was suited to peacetime conditions. And may we turn to what Mr. Karadzic says.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Having heard from the witness that he knows about this document, I don't see much of the point of reading out all those quotes, you can put your case in a succinct manner to the witness and then you can decide what to do afterward.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you remember and do you agree that we published in the papers, proclaimed and sent officially to the Party of Democratic Action and the HDZ a request for them to repeal their decision, withdraw their decision that we considered to be unlawful and unconstitutional, and that we waited for them to do that until the 24th of October?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think the -- this -- this dead-line was, in fact, seven days, but the dead-line was to expire, as I recall, at 5.00 p.m. on the 24th of October, just an hour before you had scheduled the meeting of the -- first meeting of the Bosnian Serb Assembly.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I tender this document into evidence now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit D294.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May we have 1D1411 next, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I don't know if it's been translated, but you speak our language, so just take a brief look at what it says and we can see that it was published in the media, and you're quite right, the dead-line was from the 15th to the 25th of October. Does it say here request for --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Ms. Edgerton.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Also not notified to the Prosecution, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I note it's now being repeated.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, our team members who will no longer be paid are now looking for work. Quite literally. In the literal sense, they're looking for work, so we're facing difficulties, but I think we did send this by e-mail.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: That is beside the point. You do your best to inform the Prosecution of the documents in the future. Let's move on.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Now let's see. You said that the dead-line was until 1700 hours; right?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It appears I was correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you want me to read out the first sentence? Journalists requested that Dr. Karadzic should more closely explain his statement whereby a constitutional order should be established in BiH by 1700 hours. We said that publicly. They violated the constitution in a brutal manner, and they proclaimed the Assembly session at an illegal meeting. Now, do you remember that we questioned the right for the vice-president of the Assembly to be able to call an Assembly session? Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do. This, I take it, is from the SDS party newspaper; is that correct? From "Javnost"?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: No, this is "Politika."

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can we have the top now? Can we have the very top of the page? Let me read the title and what it says. It says, "Request to annul unlawful decisions." Isn't that right? You speak our language. You can understand this.

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what the headline says, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, now let's see what it says underneath: "If this is not done by the set time, and if constitutional order is not established in Bosnia-Herzegovina, an Assembly of the Serb people in Bosnia-Herzegovina will be proclaimed consisting of its legitimate representatives"; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think you just read it, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this document be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We'll mark it for identification.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As MFI D295, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 1D01362, please. 1D01362. It hasn't been translated. We do not see that there is a translation, but this is a session of the Presidency of Bosnia-Herzegovina held on the 15th of October. That is to say, immediately after the Assembly meeting, the meeting of the Assembly of Bosnia-Herzegovina. Page 31, please. Can we have page 43, actually. It says page 43 at the bottom. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Dr. Donia, I would like to draw your attention to what it was that Professor Plavsic said. She says that the police is checking military transports, that they're working unlawfully. And now what does it say here? As for the Crisis Staff on which I was at first, the one that had been established by the Presidency, in the belief that the Crisis Staff would deal with the problem of refugees that we have in the republic and in order to allow these people to have at least a semblance of a normal life, and so on and so forth, and then part of the Presidency took over some of the authority that is otherwise vested in the council for the constitutional order. And then I saw that the Crisis Staff was debating such issues, and then I resigned from that Crisis Staff, and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I'm not sure whether Dr. Donia has been following. I think it should show the upper part.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's around the 20th line here. It has to do with the Crisis Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You see that, Dr. Donia? In the middle of the first paragraph?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And what is your question, Mr. Karadzic?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I just want to say this: The Crisis Staff should really deal with the problems that are outside the scope of a federal institutional that is called the JNA. Do you see now that this crisis in the Presidency had been a protracted one and that the Serb representatives were protesting strongly against unlawful conduct?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Dr. Karadzic, I'm going to question the authenticity of this document. It is actually a publication that was put together from a publication, and you haven't showed me the title page or the source, put together by a group of people around Miroslav Tudjman, and it was noted in the preparation of this that it was subject to editing and, furthermore, subject to the use of headlines and highlighting to make the specific didactic points involved in the text that was presented. It's -- since these clearly are transcripts that are available, I'm wondering why I'm not looking at an actual document rather than a possibly edited version of the -- of the transcript of the Presidency. I see what you've just read and note that you have read it, but I don't know that I can go any further than that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I believe that the distinguished Ms. Edgerton had confirmed on earlier occasions the authenticity of these transcripts. These are tape recordings, and they were not edited in any way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Ms. Uertz-Retzlaff.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I recall that we had this situation already at an earlier stage with another witness, and on this occasion we double checked with the Presidency minutes and found that the document and the parts that were in this book were correct. So my proposal would also be to again check -- double-check it. We will probably be able to find this very session and then see whether it's correct or not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You know, I find it irregular that I'm being shown a document for which there is a more authentic, genuine source and not the actual authoritative version which is obviously available to both sides.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well. Please continue, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can we have the next page, please, and we see towards the bottom -- actually can we scroll down so that Dr. Donia can see that this is Mr. Izetbegovic's reply. Now let us move on to the next page. Somewhere around the third of the page. The third. I think that it's in bold anyway. Actually, the sentence before that. We are fully aware of the fact that by declaring the neutrality of Bosnia-Herzegovina we may have indirectly violated some laws. However, at this point in time everything is a bit fluid. There are laws and there are laws. Do you see that Mr. Izetbegovic thought that there were laws that didn't have to be observed?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So what does it mean when he says that there are laws and there are laws? And he says, "We may have violated some laws indirectly."

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't accept that as an authoritative statement that he did.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Scroll down a bit. A bit further down.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: "We are aware that there are certain things there that constitute a violation of certain federal laws," do you see that sentence? "We are aware of the fact that there are some things there that constitute a violation of some federal laws," do you see that sentence?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't, I'm afraid.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Let's follow it. One, two -- line six from the bottom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, can I suggest to you that you just leave this matter aside and then given Ms. Uertz-Retzlaff's comment that she would double-check the authenticity or correctness of this quote. So wait until she comes back to it and then proceed to another topic first. Or you can bring up the real transcript of this. Let's move on to another topic for the time being.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Just for the very end, were you aware of the fact that Bosnia-Herzegovina or some of its institutions were violating laws?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, that's a matter of interpreting not only laws but the constitution, and the constitution court certainly ruled that certain bodies were violating laws and, in fact, certain bodies were illegal, including the SAOs and the Croatian associations that were created on the 12th and 19th of November, and that the SDS rejected the suggestion of referring the question that was debated on the 15th of October to the constitutional court. So I again will say the determination of what was legal and what was illegal was very much in the eyes of the beholder. That split took place more or less along party lines, and there was almost a unanimous reluctance to refer matters in contest to the appropriate courts.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we go back to 11306 for a moment. That is 294. Actually, our document that was admitted. Do you agree that Petko Cancar was president of the Chamber of Municipalities, one of the two Chambers in the Assembly of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know -- I didn't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
