I think the -- my view of the A/B document remains the same, that it was a critical part but only a part of an extended planning process which brought the SDS and its affiliated Serb nationalist organisations to a state of high readiness to seize power.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And after this that you had seen, Mr. Donia, you think that the Serbs on the 19th of December, even if -- well, I'm sorry that the SDS had not formed that. We're not smart enough to have done that. This has to do with a military smartness. You are trying to say that after all of this secret military activity on the part of the SDA the Serb people were supposed to wait for the Almighty to save them and not to carry out any kind of self defence. Is that what you're trying to say?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't believe this was an appropriate response to what was going on. You know, I think looking at this document, we really don't have a very good sense of how active and widespread these activities were, and so it's really not possible to say. You had a much better sense of that, I think, with your ability to weigh these things. You had a better sense of that than I would sitting here today. The -- as I say, the fact that the Patriotic League was organised, the fact that it was gaining strength and units and spreading activities starting in September of 1991, I don't -- not only do I not contest that, I've described it in some of my writings.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can these two documents, actually paper A and B, and this one, can they be admitted. Oh, A and B have been admitted. So can this paper be admitted, the one that we just had on our screens now. 107.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: What is the exhibit number of 225, Variant A and B? Is that the exhibit number? Ms. Edgerton.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: P0005. Maybe I've missed one zero, but --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: P5. And I take it there's no objection in admitting this Halilovic promotion document.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: No. No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The first page of the B/C/S hasn't been translated. Would you like to insert that as well?

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Izetbegovic's decision, yes. So we'll mark it for identification pending --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think it has been translated, Excellency. 1D108. That's a separate document. This is a decision in relation to that request.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, but we'd like to see that decision as well, because it's there in B/C/S. So we'll mark it for identification pending the translation of the first page of the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be MFI D298.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, I'm noting the time. What subject matters are there that remain to be cross-examined?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, believe me, you know, the extent to which Mr. Donia's work has been incorporated in the indictment. We are on the eve of the new year. We're dealing with the 21st and 22nd of December. While we're talking, 1D855, I'd like to have of that called up so Mr. Donia can see how extensive this activity was. We've dealt with Variant A and B and then comes the establishment of Republika Srpska, then our participation in the work of the parliament on the 24th and 25th of January, yet another attempt to save Bosnia, and then the international conference, the Carrington-Cutileiro Conference and then we are getting close to March, the armed attack against Bosanski Brod, the 18th of March, there was the agreement. And then on the 25th of March, they give up on the agreement. And then comes the 1st of April, from the 1st until the 5th of April, there is the crisis in Bijeljina, the crisis in Kupres, and so on and so forth. So from this sequence of events that Mr. Donia has been speaking about, in a very arbitrary way in my opinion, I am brought into a situation whereby I have to extend my defence activities. After that, we have to do with the roots of the activity of the peoples Assembly. Mr. Donia wrote an entire paper on that. And finally we come to Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The Chamber will confer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: With the indulgence of the interpreters, we'll go till 2.00, if it is okay with the doctor again. And then, Mr. Karadzic, you will have two sessions tomorrow. That's the ruling, and you should plan your cross-examination to be able to conclude by the end of second session tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Donia, I would like to draw your attention to this report of Memic, Senaid, son of Hasan who armed Muslims in the area of Sarajevo. This is his statement. The first paragraph, the underlined bit. Actually we can look at the hole thing. In the period from September 1991 up to my arrest, I had, for the purposes of the SDA in Bosnia-Herzegovina and Sandzak, purchased, imported and distributed around 5.000 automatic rifles and rifles of various types and around 1.400.000 bullets. I had done all of that in co-operation with SDA activists on the ground, as ordered by certain leaders of the SDA. My closest ties in this job were with Hasan Cengic, who is otherwise a technical secretary of the SDA. All leaders of the political life of the SDA were aware of my dealings such as Alija Izetbegovic, Omer Behmen, Rusmir Mahmutcehajic and others as well as certain officials of the MUP of Bosnia-Herzegovina, the MUP minister, Alija Delimustafic; deputy staff minister, Mirsad Srebrenikovic; Jusuf Pusina; Bakir Alispahic; Kemal Sabuvic [phoen]; Momir Alibabic, as well as some SJB operatives throughout Bosnia. You see that only this one person brought in 5.000 rifles and one and a half million bullets.

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'd like to see the nature of this document further. I'm afraid I don't see whether it's signed, whether it's -- what its origin is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, sir, this is a police telegram. They are -- it was handwritten, and this -- and we have that. This is a telegram whereby the regional police station is providing information about this. They actually copied his statement, and we actually have that in -- handwritten as it is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Can you give the foundation as to this document, the context in which this Mr. Memic --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have page 4 so that Mr. Donia can see that this is a statement of Senaid Memic, an arrested person who made a statement to police organs. And this is the form of telegram that the police use. It's done using their own machinery. Not anybody can do that. Can we go to the end of this handwritten document. I think that it is signed on each page. I think that his signature is on each and every page.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Ms. Edgerton.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Just related to what Mr. Karadzic said, which police body? I see no indication.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's the 14th of April, 1992, war activities are underway and this is the police in Ilidza, I assume. If we can have the last page, then we're going to see his signature.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We are seeing the last page, but --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we scroll down so we see his signature?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: That's the bottom part, as far as -- but what's the point. What is your question? Put it to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Have you heard of Senad Sahinpasic whom we did mention during your cross?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, without knowing much of anything about him.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could we have page 2 in English. See, here on page 2 it says that: "I know that in addition to myself, Senad Sahinpasic, Alija Delimustafic's partner, procured weapons for the SDA," and so on and so forth. So do you think -- or, rather, did you know that this activity was going on in the area of Sarajevo in this way?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I -- I see no basis for affirming anything in this document. I don't see its origin. I don't know -- the signature that you're talking about doesn't seem to appear. I'm not even sure if it did come from the police station in Ilidza what the -- who controlled that police station as of the 14th of April, whether it was the SDS or whether it was the government of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, sir, the SDS did not have its own police stations. The police station is a police station. The top people of that police station were not SDS members. Haven't we established that?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this document be admitted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. 1D77 then, please. This is a document that we have already shown, but we did not tender it. This is a Muslim document, a Muslim document from 1993. Can we have the next page now, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: The last paragraph says: "However, from the very beginning, major influence in Foca was exercised by Senad Sahinpasic, Saja, and Halid Cengic, who are related to," et cetera, et cetera. Yes, yes we can keep the English where it is. This document speaks of their procurement of weapons and also the fact that they sold 5.200 rifles in Foca at a price of about 1.200 Deutschmark each. Are you doubting that as well?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Less so.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this document be admitted into evidence? We've already shown it, but we haven't tendered it yet.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Edgerton.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: I don't think there's any foundation based on Dr. Donia's answer for the admission of this document, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The answer, "less so."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BAIRD
utterances.text: Dr. Donia, what do you mean by "less so"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I mean I doubt it less so. It appears to be a genuine product of the security services of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina. I'm just having -- not surveyed the whole document, I can't really comment on it. I note, for example, at the very bottom of this page there's a statement that in April 1992 the Chetniks attacked Foca in the empty-handed and disorganised Muslim people had no choice but to leave their homes and wander. That to me is a kind of a -- such a vague statement as to have no -- no value in a document like that. First of all, it's highly tendentious and very vague. So I would want to look at the whole thing before I, let's say, affirmed anything that's stated here as -- as likely to be the case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The Chamber will admit this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: My position, Mr. Donia, was that you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The Chamber has given its ruling. We'll admit it.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D299, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Your last question for today, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 1D184. Could I call that up, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: While we're waiting for that document, Mr. Donia, as for the Serb National Council founded before the elections, you said that it hadn't done much, that somehow they were in abeyance. Do you know that it is now a legal obligation for every ethnic community to have their own National Council?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean in Bosnia today?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In Serbia. In Serbia. But I believe that that will be the case in Bosnia too. That is a recommendation of the European Union.

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it's -- I think it's a recommendation of the European Union or one of several things that the European Union kind of sets out as a -- as a standard, but I'm not aware of -- I'm just not aware of a requirement that every body have its national defence -- or I'm sorry, National Council. The National Council we're talking about you proclaimed in Banja Luka, I think on October 12th or something like that of 1991, and you were the -- the SDS was the only party that established such a council prior to the election, and it was, I think, viewed as an act of bad faith to do that unilaterally, but at the same time for whatever reason it never did much. It never took on a life of its own and seemed to be a body that you sort of mentioned from time to time, perhaps held in abeyance, but didn't really ever assume any functions.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. My point, Mr. Donia, is that all our bodies that were being established were being established in case we have to use them. For a long time they were on standby, as it were. So do you see this document dated the 17 of January? Do you agree that we continued to take part in the political life of Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Do I agree that you continued to take part in the political life in Bosnia? Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes. You read our language. This is a press conference that was attended by Professor Plavsic and Professor Koljevic, and can't you see that we are saying not partition but transformation of Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In fact, transformation of Bosnia was kind of a -- I would say a buzzword, frequently used slogan which was essentially a way of saying the division of Bosnia into three separate sovereign polities. It was the knew programme that I see you having espoused in the aftermath of the events of the 15th of October, 1991. This is from "Politika," so would I not put a whole lot of credence in -- in what's here, but usually at such press conferences the quotations are accurate, so I would not [overlapping speakers].

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You, Mr. Donia, would not believe the Serbs anything, but I'm asking you, isn't what is written here is not partition but transformation and also the fact that we advocated Bosnia as a Switzerland? Are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I am, and I don't believe it's correct for you to say that I wouldn't believe anything Serbs said. I believe a lot of things that Serbs said, including some things that you say. I don't believe everything that you say, but I do accept at face value many things that you say, and I also believe what people in -- the Serbs and the non-nationalist parties say from time to time but not exclusively. I don't -- I don't accept that I'm just not prepared to believe anything you say.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: That's it for today. Mr. Karadzic, bear that in mind, that you will have only two sessions tomorrow and a further extension will not be allowed. We will admit this document. We'll mark it for identification, D300 MFI.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm sorry about that. I'll do my best, but I will consider the situation to be that this witness had not been fully cross-examined.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Tomorrow we are sitting in the afternoon, 2.15.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 10th day of January, 2010, at 2.15 p.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 2.02 p.m.,
